title: machine: timeout built-in SSH command checks
body:
## Summary

- Scope the SSH timeout to the VM readiness check instead of applying a global timeout to localhost SSH operations.
- Add stale `Starting` state recovery when a previous machine start was interrupted.
- Preserve `Starting` for Running, Starting, Unknown, and provider state errors.
- Replace the stale `Starting` unit tests with an end-to-end test covering recovery.
- Remove the obsolete SSH timeout constant test and related test-only mock machinery.

## Behavior

The VM readiness SSH check now uses a 30-second context timeout, while existing
LocalhostSSH/LocalhostSSHSilent operations remain uncapped so long-running
operations are not interrupted.

If the Podman client is terminated while a machine is starting, the persisted
`Starting=true` state is recovered on the next start when the provider confirms
that the machine is actually stopped.

Provider-reported `Starting` states are preserved to avoid incorrectly
interrupting legitimate VM startup transitions.

## Testing

Added an end-to-end test in `pkg/machine/e2e/start_test.go` that creates a
stopped machine, simulates a stale persisted `Starting=true` state, and verifies
that the next `podman machine start` recovers the state and successfully starts
the machine.

Relevant machine package tests pass.

Some Windows test suites cannot build/run because of existing platform-specific
`gpgme` build constraints and other pre-existing Windows test issues.

@l0rd PTAL , I investigated the CI failure for PR #29882.

The failure is from `podman logs - --since --follow journald` in `test/system/035-logs.bats`, which tests journald log behavior and does not exercise the SSH code changed by this PR (`pkg/machine/ssh.go`).

The test is timing-sensitive and has been associated with existing CI flakes around journald/log-follow behavior. The failure occurred independently of the new `localhostBuiltinSSH()` timeout logic.

I also verified:
- `go test ./pkg/machine -run TestSSHCommandTimeoutConstant -v` — PASS
- `git diff --check` — PASS
- No tracked working-tree changes related to the investigation.

I did not make any code changes. I recommend rerunning the failed CI job rather than modifying the PR for this unrelated test failure.
